Thus Dobraeus for τοῦ δ᾽ ἀγκυλητοῦ κοσσάβιός ἐστι σκοπός [and the target of the curved cottabus is], which is read in Athenaeus 15 p. 667c. But the same author in 11 p. 782 e mentions τοὺς ἀγκυλητοὺς κοττάβους [the curved cottabi] from Aeschylus. In the preceding verse Dobraeus rightly corrected ἦν μὲν γὰρ αὐτῷ σκοπὸς ἀεὶ τοὐμὸν κάρα [for his target was always my head] for ἦν μὲν γὰρ αὐτῷ κότταβος τοὐμὸν κάρα [for his cottabus was my head].

It is a weightier word than ὀργή [anger] and is used especially of anger stored deep in the mind or long cherished: see Thes. vol. 4 p. 1878. Sophocles never used this word; it occurs once in Euripides Rhes. 827 μὴ κότον μοι ἐφῆς [do not lay up wrath against me], very often in Aeschylus.

where the sense requires another word, such as ποτῷ [drink], which Auratus conjectured, or κύτει με [with a vessel me] according to Scaliger. In another way it is corrupt at 1641 ὁ δυσφιλής κότῳ λιμός ξύνοικος [the hateful famine dwelling with wrath], where Pearson rightly has δυσφιλής σκότῳ [hateful in darkness], except that it is better to write δυσφιλεῖ [hateful] with Stanley.
